data.name: TipPriceUnit
data.value: The unit prices are written in: Exalted or Chaos Orbs. From one Divine Orb on they are always in Divine. The price floor above has its own unit.

data.name: TipVersion
data.value: What changed in this version: the changelog on github.com (opens in your browser).

data.name: TipExtendedDiagnostics
data.value: For bug reports: the program also keeps pictures of moments it decided on its own, a few of each kind, in the diagnostics folder. Off: only the diagnostics key writes there. Nothing is sent anywhere either way.

data.name: CloseHint
data.value: Closing the window minimizes to tray. Use Exit to quit.

data.name: TipFloor
data.value: Applies to Favours, Remnant rewards (value of the whole row) and stash tabs (price per item). Below the threshold, Favours and stash items show a grey "<"; Remnants show nothing. Does not affect the green top-price highlight.

data.name: TipHotkey
data.value: Click the field, then press a key or key combination. Only active while PoE 2 is in the foreground.

data.name: TipAutoScan
data.value: Shows prices automatically for the checked windows while they are open. The hotkey always shows all of them; with none checked, prices appear on hotkey only.

data.name: TipIntervals
data.value: If the game stutters, increase both intervals. The first applies while no window is shown, the second while one is shown (prices then disappear correspondingly later). Minimum: {0} s and {1} s; maximum for the second: {2} s. Values outside these limits are adjusted on save.

data.name: TipStartWithWindows
data.value: Adds poe2pricer to Windows startup for this user account; it then starts in the tray, without a window. Applied or removed on save.

data.name: TipCheckForUpdates
data.value: Asks github.com once at every start whether a newer version is on the Releases page; nothing else is sent, and nothing is downloaded or installed without your click. A newer version is shown in the status line and as a tray message.

data.name: TextRecognitionOffer
data.value:
poe2pricer needs the English text recognition of Windows (language feature “English (United States)”). It is not installed on this computer.
Install it now? Windows asks for administrator rights and downloads it; this needs an internet connection and may take a few minutes.
Without it poe2pricer cannot start.

data.name: TextRecognitionFailed
data.value:
The text recognition could not be installed ({0}).
You can install it yourself: Windows Settings → Time & language → Language & region → Add a language → English (United States), with “Optical character recognition” ticked. Then start poe2pricer again.

data.name: TextRecognitionRestart
data.value: The text recognition is installed. Please start poe2pricer again.

data.name: TextRecognitionWindowsRestart
data.value: The text recognition is installed, but Windows needs a restart to finish it. Restart Windows by Settings → Windows Update → Restart now (a restart from the Start menu may put it off), then start poe2pricer again.

data.name: TextRecognitionRestartPending
data.value: Windows is waiting for a restart to finish an update; until then it cannot install the English text recognition. Restart Windows by Settings → Windows Update → Restart now, then start poe2pricer again. If the text recognition is still missing then, poe2pricer offers to install it.

data.name: TextRecognitionInstalling
data.value: Installing the English text recognition. Windows first checks its optional features (the long part), then downloads the feature, then installs it; measured 3 to 10 minutes. poe2pricer starts by itself when it is done. This window can be minimised.

data.name: TextRecognitionCancelled

data.value: The expedition tier of an island is the mean of these weights over every rumour seen there (custom tiers count first), shown as the highest tier the mean reaches. Applied on save.

data.name: TipTabletKind
data.value: The kind of tablet. Each kind has one profile of its own; the fields below belong to the kind chosen here, and a kind with a profile is marked in the list. ✕ clears the fields.

data.name: TipTabletRemoveProfile
data.value: Clear the fields: the kind has no profile then, and its tablets are priced exactly by their own mods

data.name: TipTabletTolerance
data.value: In percent. A mod's own value on the tablet, lowered by this much, is the minimum the trade site is asked for: 36 with 10 % asks for 33 or more, 2 stays 2. A profile's minimum counts as met when the value is not more than this much under it.

data.name: TipTabletUses
data.value: A tablet starts with 10 uses and loses one per map. The trade site is asked for tablets with at least this many left; the search text and the tooltip's judgement take it as well.

data.name: TipTabletMods
data.value: Four mods a group at most, as many as a tablet carries

data.name: TipTablets
data.value: The search text goes into the search box of a stash tab: it highlights the tablets of this kind that match the profile. The price is the cheapest tablet of the kind the profile describes on the trade site of pathofexile.com (no uniques), asked with "Refresh price" only. At a tooltip the profile names what is asked for; a kind without a profile is asked for exactly as the tablet is. The site states a limit of a few requests per ten seconds; the program keeps under it.

data.name: TipAddGroup
data.value: A new group right after this one; its rows count together by its kind, the groups all together.

data.name: TipRemoveGroup
data.value: Remove this group with its rows

data.name: TipGroupKind
data.value: and: every row of the group is required. or: at least one row of the group will do. not: none of the rows may be there. All groups together must hold.

data.name: UnsavedProfile
data.value: "{0}" has changes that are not saved. Save them before you leave it?

data.name: TipExactPriceKey
data.value: At a waystone's or tablet's tooltip: its live price asked exactly as the item is, every value and every mod, past the profiles. Until the mouse or cursor leaves the item. Click the field, then press a key or key combination.

data.name: TradeBusy
data.value: trade site busy, again in {0} s

data.name: ExactKeyTaken
data.value: The key {0} to force a live price is already one of the other two keys, so it is off. Set a free key in the settings window.

data.name: TipCaptureGameWindow
data.value: The game is read from its own window, so the prices stay out of the program's view by themselves and recording software (NVIDIA app, OBS, Game Bar) can record the desktop and shows the prices. Off: the screen is read and the prices are hidden from every recording. Needs Windows 11; on Windows 10 the screen is read. Reading the window is also the cheaper way (about 2 ms a look instead of 8).

data.name: CaptureFellBack
data.value: Capturing the game window gave no picture; reading the screen instead until the next start. Recordings won't show the prices meanwhile.

data.name: CaptureUnavailable
data.value: This Windows can't capture the game window without a frame around it (that needs Windows 11); reading the screen instead. Recordings won't show the prices.

data.name: TipTradeInPerson
data.value: Which offers on the trade site count for every waystone and tablet price, live and in the tabs. By default only Instant Buyout: what Ange sells from merchant tabs, bought at once even while the seller is offline. Ticked: also items in premium stash tabs whose seller is online (whisper and trade in person). Offline sellers never count: their listings are often months old and long sold.

data.name: WaystoneSearchTooLong
data.value: Too long for the game's search box: drop a mod or a value.

data.name: TipWaystoneTolerance
data.value: In percent. The waystone's own values, each lowered by this much, are the minimum the trade site is asked for: 59 % rarity with 10 % asks for 54 % or more. A profile's minimum counts as met when the value is not more than this much under it. Mods the profile excludes are excluded there too.

data.name: TipWaystones
data.value: The search text goes into the search box of a stash tab: it highlights the waystones that match the profile. The price is the cheapest waystone the profile describes on the trade site of pathofexile.com, asked with "Refresh price" only (Instant Buyout; with "incl. premium stash (online)" in the settings also sellers who are online). The site states a limit of a few requests per ten seconds; the program keeps under it and asks the price of a waystone once every ten minutes at most.

data.name: TipWaystoneFilter
data.value: Type a part of the mod's text: the list shows only mods that hold it.

data.name: TipWaystoneProfile
data.value: The saved profiles. Type a new name to start a profile from the fields as they stand; it is saved with Save. ✕ removes the chosen profile.

data.name: TipWaystoneSaveProfile
data.value: Save this profile (the profiles are saved apart from the program settings)

data.name: TipWaystoneRefreshPrice
data.value: Ask the trade site for the cheapest item the profile describes. Only this button asks: the site allows a few requests in ten seconds, and the live price in the game needs them too.

data.name: LiveTradePrice
data.value: Live price from the trade site

data.name: TipLiveTradePrice
data.value: Live price at the tooltip of a waystone or tablet: the trade site is asked for the cheapest offer like it, and the price stands at the right end of the title bar. Off: nothing is asked and nothing drawn at the tooltip; the key "Force live price" asks all the same.

data.name: NoticeText
data.value:
poe2pricer is a third-party tool for Path of Exile 2. Before you run it beside the game, know what it does.
• It reads the picture of the game window and draws prices over it: by itself when one of the windows opens, or on Alt+F, as you set it in Settings. • It presses no keys and clicks nothing. • It does not open the game's process, read its memory or change its files. The one file it reads is the game's settings file, for text size and language. • It never connects to the game servers. Its requests go to poe.ninja and poecdn (prices and item art), the trade site, the community rumour table (gnejs.app and a public Google sheet) and GitHub. • Grinding Gear Games approves no third-party tool and may act against any account at its discretion. Nobody can promise that a tool stays tolerated. You run it at your own risk.
What GGG has said about third-party tools, with the sources, and what that means for this program: Help → "Third-party tools and GGG".
